newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium plans more contact with Zaire's Kabila.
newsitem.headline: Belgium plans more contact with Zaire's Kabila.

text.p: Belgium plans further contacts with Laurent Kabila, the rebel leader who has captured about a quarter of Belgium's former colony Zaire, the foreign ministry said on Wednesday.
On Tuesday, the Belgian government had a first official contact with Kabila in his eastern Zaire stronghold Kisangani.

Christian Monnoyer, the foreign ministry's Africa specialist, told Kabila that Belgian troops now in Brazzaville in neighbouring Congo would only be used to evacute Belgian nationals and would not to meddle in Zairean politics or support Zairean president Mobutu Sese Seko.

A foreign ministry spokesman said on Wednesday that Yves Haesendonck, Belgium's ambassador for the Great Lakes region, would see Zaireans "from all parties involved, including (Kabila's) ADFL" in Lome, Togo, where Organisation of African Unity (OAU) foreign minsiters are to broker a truce in Zaire.
Kabila, leader of the Alliance of Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Congo-Zaire (ADFL), lashed out at Belgium lasat week for not having made official contact with him.
France -- despite its support for the ailing Mobutu, whom Kabila wants to overthrow -- has already sent envoys to Kabila.

Haesendonck has met United Nations representative Mohamed Sahnoun and European Union envoy Aldo Ajello and will also talk to French and U.S. representatives about a peace agreement in the vast central African country.
The U.S., France and Belgium have massed about 1,000 troops in Brazzaville, ready to evacuate their nationals from Kinshasa if necessary.
